results.summary: This project implements a tiny Snake game on a 7-segment LED display, combined with an 8-state finite state machine (PRISM). The game speed is controlled by the 8-bit ui_in input, with larger values meaning slower speed. It requires only the 7-segment display on the demo board and a 10 kHz clock. The design is a simple Wokwi example that demonstrates two different designs in one, but changing from slow to fast speed may cause a delay due to the simple equality-based speed comparison.

This design creates a Cylon scanner effect by sequentially lighting eight LEDs in a back-and-forth pattern. It uses an 8-bit shift register with direction control and turn-around detection, requiring eight LEDs with resistors and a reset switch. The clock can range from about 1 Hz to MHz, with 4-8 Hz being optimal. The project is a simple Wokwi example that demonstrates a classic LED scanning effect.

This is a 16-bit Data General Nova 1200 CPU implemented with a 4-bit nibble-serial datapath, capable of executing programs stored in external QSPI Flash and using PSRAM for data storage. It includes a UART for serial communication at 19,200 baud and drives diagnostic blinkenlights on the 7-segment display. The design requires the official Tiny Tapeout QSPI PMOD for Flash and PSRAM, and programs are written in Nova assembly and flashed via a provided Python script. Notable features include full programmability and interactive terminal I/O, though it relies on external hardware for memory and communication.

This project implements a DTMF (Touch-Tone) decoder that identifies telephone keypad tones using the Goertzel algorithm to perform a discrete Fourier transform. It accepts 8-bit audio samples at 44.1 kHz via a ready-valid handshake and outputs the detected row and column indices after processing 1024 samples. The design requires an external audio source and a clock of 50 MHz, and it uses a bit-serial multiplier that may introduce latency between samples. It is a specialized DSP application for decoding standard DTMF signals.
